Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as it may be visible to other participants. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Mike Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: Operating margin by segment (if applicable), Strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter/year, Trends in staffing levels and contract labor usage, Status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures, Same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter/year, and Overview of key financial performance highlights. These areas highlight our disciplined approach to growth and profitability in a dynamic healthcare environment. I'll touch on them at a high level now, and David will provide deeper insights shortly.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to David Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

David Chen:
Thank you, Mike, and good morning, everyone. As Mike mentioned, we had a solid quarter across the board. Let me kick things off with a high-level overview of our key financial performance highlights. Overall, we delivered strong results, with total net revenues reaching $4.52 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year. This growth was propelled by robust same-hospital volume increases, positive shifts in payer mix, and contributions from our recent ambulatory surgery center tuck-ins. Adjusted EBITDA hit $485 million, reflecting a 12.5% rise from Q3 2023, with margins widening 110 basis points to 17.0%. This extends our streak to 10 straight quarters of EBITDA expansion, demonstrating the strength of our asset-light outpatient focus even as we face labor pressures and Medicare reimbursement challenges.

Diving into the details, net patient revenues, making up 92% of total, climbed 7.9% to $4.16 billion. Same-hospital admissions rose 4.1% year-over-year to 142,000, surpassing the 2.8% industry average per American Hospital Association data for acute care. Average daily census increased 3.2% to 2,450 beds across our 45-hospital network, with average length of stay steady at 4.7 days. Case mix index edged up to 1.85 from 1.82, driven by higher-acuity cardiology and orthopedics cases, bolstered by partnerships with Medtronic and Stryker on advanced robotics like Mazor X and Rosa systems.

Outpatient volumes excelled, up 11.6% on a same-facility basis, tracking the shift to site-neutral payments and value-based arrangements. Revenue per outpatient visit grew 6.3% to $1,420, thanks to premium procedures in ASCs and hospital outpatient departments. Outpatient now accounts for 42% of net patient revenues, up from 38% last year and ahead of peers like HCA Healthcare. This stems from our $250 million Outpatient Acceleration Program last year, featuring de novo ASC builds in Sun Belt markets and inpatient bed conversions to procedural suites.

Expenses were well-controlled, with total operating costs up 6.8% to $3.67 billion, under our guidance, due to supply chain gains and Epic EHR enhancements. Labor, at 52% of revenues, rose 7.2% but slowed from Q2's 9.1% via retention bonuses and a 15% drop in agency spend through our HealthBridge TalentHub platform. Non-labor costs increased 5.9%, offset by 8% supply deflation via Vizient GPO rebates on ortho implants and pharmaceuticals.

Our 17.0% adjusted EBITDA margins gained 220 basis points from payer mix improvements and leverage. Commercial managed care hit 58% of mix, up 200 basis points, with 4.5% average rate hikes from UnitedHealthcare and Anthem deals. Medicare at 28% dealt with a 2.9% IPPS update and 1.2% sequestration, but strong value-based purchasing scores of 85/100 limited penalties. Medicaid at 14% gained from Texas and Florida supplements.

Regionally, the Southeast—Florida, Texas, Georgia with 60% of beds—fueled 65% of growth, with same-hospital net revenue per admission up 9.1% to $15,200 on 5.8% volumes. Florida's demographics and post-hurricane recovery boosted ortho and neuro, while Texas' new Level II trauma center added 1,200 patient days. Northeast sites in New York and Pennsylvania grew softer at 2.3% from payer issues, but a new Empire BlueCross deal restores 3.5% rates.

These outcomes affirm our High-Growth, High-Margin strategy. We've added three $180 million ASC bolt-ons for 20%+ EBITDA yields, growing our ASCs to 28. AI revenue cycle tools with Change Healthcare cut A/R days to 42 from 48, freeing $65 million cash. Telehealth reached 28% of outpatient visits from 22%. Sustainability efforts like LED retrofits and solar at 15 hospitals trimmed utilities 12% for ESG financing.

Our balance sheet is solid: net debt to EBITDA at 3.1x from 3.4x, $1.2 billion liquidity. Capex $210 million targeted capacity and digital, including $50 million Nuance Dragon Ambient eXperience rollout. Free cash flow $320 million backs $0.45 dividend and $300 million buybacks.

We reaffirm FY2024 guidance: revenues $11.4-$11.6 billion, EBITDA $1.95-$2.00 billion, EPS $4.80-$5.00. Q4 same-hospital admissions 3.5-4.5%, margins 16.8-17.3%.

Net revenue for Q3 was $4.52 billion, up 8% from last year, fueled by patient volumes, payer mix, and revenue cycle gains. Operating expenses totaled $3.67 billion, or 81% of net revenue. We're prioritizing cost control while investing in growth, especially supply chain digitization. Net income was $250 million, or $1.20 per share. We're confident in hitting yearly goals.

Now, I'll dive into operating margins by segment, which showcase our diversified portfolio's strength amid macro and regulatory pressures. Operating margin uses adjusted operating income over segment revenue, sans one-offs. Consolidated margins hit 13.2% for Q3, up 110 basis points YoY and 50 sequentially, from cost discipline, procedure mix, and AI revenue cycle via Epic and Cerner.

Acute Care Hospitals, 62% of revenue at $2.8 billion from 45 facilities in 12 states, Sun Belt heavy like Texas, Florida, Arizona akin to HCA. Margins rose to 10.5%, +70 bps YoY from 9.8%, +40 bps QoQ. Admissions +4.2% YoY on ortho, cardio, neuro; CMI +2.1% to 1.85 post-COVID. Labor up 6% on RN shortages—agency at 12% hours—but offset by Care at Scale cross-training and Aya partnerships. Supplies 22% revenue flat via Vizient GPO, $45M savings. Payer mix 45% Medicare, 25% Medicaid, 30% commercial; FY24 IPPS -2.7%. Sunbelt 12.1% vs. Midwest 8.9%, uncompensated down 15%. Target 11.5% year-end via 68% bed use, tele-ICU in 10 sites.

Outpatient Services, 18% or $820 million, topped at 18.2% margins, +140 bps YoY, +90 QoQ, beating Surgery Partners benchmarks. Revenue +12% on 9% volumes in ASCs/imaging, same-facility 8.5%. Site-neutral No Surprises Act aids; ortho +15%, GI +11% over 25% margins. Da Vinci in 20 ASCs +18% OR throughput. Mid-level staffing held wage inflation 4%. Southeast 35 centers at 20.1% on Florida aging, Medicare Advantage; Northeast higher malpractice. Tuck-in M&A pipeline for two ASCs, 20%+ accretive, to 22% revenue by 2025 at 19-20% margins.

Physician Practices, 12% or $540 million, margins 15.8% flat YoY +60 bps QoQ like Tenet Conifer. 2,200 providers, revenue +7% on 5% visits, 2% RVU from primary 40%, ortho/cardio 35%. Value-based 55% lives with UnitedHealthcare, Humana; $28M incentives. Change Healthcare AI cut denials 22%, A/R to 42 days. Labor +5.5% offset by scribes, telehealth 25% visits. Texas/Georgia 17.5%, California 13.2% Medi-Cal lags. Aligned models to 17% margins next year.

Behavioral Health, 8% or $360 million, 9.5% margins -50 bps YoY flat QoQ, resilient vs. UHS peers' declines. Inpatient days +3%, outpatient PHP/IOP +11% anxiety/substance. Medicare -3.2%, labor +8% psych techs; Behavioral Pathways Merative analytics cut LOS 0.8 to 8.2 days, uncompensated -18%. Southwest 11.2%, Northeast 7.8%. $50M crisis centers, Talkspace telepsych for $50B market, 11% FY25.

Overall, diversification—outpatient/physician buoy acute/behavioral—for 14%+ 2024 margins, $200M synergies GHX supply digitization, Six Sigma.

Next, trends in staffing and contract labor, key cost drivers at 52% expenses, down from 55% YoY, adding 120 bps to EBITDA margins. FTEs 48,200, +1.8% YoY with volumes; nurses 28,000 +2.2% matching 3.1% patient days; physicians flat 4,800 via hospitalists/tele-ICU; support +1.5%. Turnover 14% from 28%, nurses 16% from 32%, like HCA's 15.5%, Advisory Board RN vacancies 9% from 18%.

Contract labor down to 3.8% nursing hours from 13.5% peak, -72% YoY, expense $42M -68%, $175M savings despite +4.2% volumes. Southeast <2.5% strong pools; California 6.2% AB 2579 wages. LeanTaaS iQueue 85% hospitals -8-10% overstaffing, 12% unproductive hours. ShiftMed pilots 40% cheaper. Workday 95% census accuracy.

Nurse Horizon 1,200 RNs via schools like Grand Canyon, $15k bonuses 88% retention, $10k tuition. Locums -55% to 2.1%, ApexCare tele 22% ICU. Expect 3% contract year-end, labor inflation 3.5-4% FY24.

On M&A, core to allocation amid Medicare Advantage cuts, 5.8% labor per AHA, $100B PE powder. Ongoing: $1.2B Southeast Regional five-hospital Georgia/SC closed September post-HSR/CON; $45M synergies supply/Epic 85%; accretes $0.25 EPS FY24, commercial to 52%, readmits -2.2pts to 14.8% ACO REACH.

$325M ACN 15-ASC DFW Q4 close; ortho/GI 35% margins, JVs ortho groups 20% volumes athenahealth.

Divestitures: three Midwest rural CAHs 180 beds $150M August, $60M gain; dragged <2% margins 35% occupancy 65% Medicaid. Midwest now urban 72% occupancy 12.5% +450 bps.

Planned: $2.5B pipeline, three LOIs five diligence. $750M 12-IRF PNW stroke/neuro 1,000 beds 25% IRR bundling IRF-PPS. $200-300M Sunbelt: Florida home health 40% MA Optum tech; Texas cardio vertical 15% accretion.

60% debt 4.2%, 40% equity, $2B 2024 cap net leverage 3.2x <4.5x covenant. Consolidation up 22% Bain, Southeast overweight demographics 2.5x, Nuance AI 10-15% labor post-acquisition. 8% revenue growth, 200bps margins, $1.8B powder.

For same-facility volume/revenue guidance, excluding acquisitions like Southeast tuck-in, organic across 45 hospitals/120 ASCs 18 states. Q4 admissions 3.5-4.5% from Q3 4.2%, elective +6.1% QoQ ortho/cardio/TAVR +8% Phoenix. Inpatient days 2.8-3.5%, CMI 1.85 +1.2%. Outpatient 5-6% MSK/GI, ER 3-4% flu/RSV watch Midwest.

Revenue 4.5-5.5%, NRNA +1-1.5% 3.5% commercial escalators, FY25 IPPS +2.9%, offset Medicaid disenroll Texas/FL -50bps mix.

FY2025 admissions 4-5%, days 3.5-4.5%, outpatient 6-7% ortho/surgery 7-8%. Revenue 5-6%, NRNA +1-1.5% value-based 25% from 18% BCBS bundles.

Sunbelt 40% beds +5.2% Q3 Florida/Texas; $150M workforce AI Epic/Incredible Health -15% agency. Vizient 2-3% supply savings. Da Vinci 20 sites +12% surgical 58% OR. 30% site-neutral Tenet-like +100-150bps. Arizona +6% retirees, CA flat Medi-Cal; Midwest neuro offsets.

Risks CMS IRA site-neutral, respiratory; upside commercial/tele-onco 15%.

Finally, strategic priorities/outlook post-Q3 6.2% same-hospital revenue, 18.4% EBITDA peak three quarters. Priorities: operational excellence/margins, outpatient portfolio, digital/clinical innovation, M&A/de novo. Navigate CMS FY25 IPPS -2.8%, 4-5% labor, value-based post-elective rebound.

Operational: HRO HCA/Cleveland Clinic, CMI 1.82 +150bps, ortho/neuro +12%, beds 72% from 68%, surgical 85%. Labor 52% nurse turnover 14% from 18% $15M incentives; Vizient 7-9% savings implants/pharma. Southeast 35% beds +8% admissions offset Midwest flu.

Outpatient: ASCs 25% surgical Tenet-like; divested two rural $180M to five ASCs DFW/Phoenix 75% utilization $50M EBITDA 35% vs inpatient 15-18%. Bundled hip/knee UnitedHealthcare 20% risk Q4, value-based 15% to 25% 2026 CHS ahead.

Digital: $250M Apex Digital 18 months Epic MyChart/Nuance AI scribes -30% doc time, +15% productivity CA 10-hospital. Da Vinci Xi 20 ORs +10% throughput premium. Google Cloud LOS -0.3 to 4.1 <15% readmits. Tele 18% to RPM Livongo Medicare Advantage.

M&A/de novo: $1.2B powder Sunbelt Orlando/Nashville >2% growth; Q3 $300M three-hospital 12x accretive. De novo ASC TX/AZ +1,200 procedures 2025. Mexico JVs minor, US 95%.

Q3 guide: admissions 4-5%, revenue $2.85-2.90B +6-7%, EBITDA $520-540M 18.5-19%. FY24 revenue $11.5-11.7B +6%, EBITDA $2.15-2.20B 18.5%, 3% NRNA payer/service offset 4% labor. Capex $450M digital/outpatient.

2025: elective ortho +10-12%, MA 28%, Cures interoperability. Risks IPPS -1-2%, cyber; leverage 2.8x $800M cash for 7-9% CAGR 20%+ margins 2026.

With that, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Thank you, David. Good morning. We're advancing clinical outcomes and satisfaction. Our bundled payment program delivered a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We're harnessing technology for better patient experience and coordination, notably our telehealth platform now at 28% of visits.

Following that, Tom will update on operations.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We're streamlining across our network. Initiatives like LeanTaaS iQueue for scheduling and Vizient GPO supply negotiations yielded major savings, cutting overstaffing and supply costs significantly.

Now, over to Elena for innovation.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Tom. We're driving innovation organization-wide. Investments in technologies and partnerships enhance care, efficiency, new revenues. Projects like the Apex Digital Health Platform with Nuance AI scribes and da Vinci robotic expansions tackle clinician burnout and surgical throughput, addressing key healthcare challenges like labor shortages and procedure backlogs.

Now, back to Mike.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Elena. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of LeanTaaS iQueue?

Tom Hargrove:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. LeanTaaS iQueue, rolled out to 85% of our hospitals, uses AI predictive analytics for nurse scheduling, reducing overstaffing by 8-10% per shift and unproductive hours by 12%. This sustained our CMS star ratings above 4.2 while contributing to our 120 basis point EBITDA lift this quarter, with ongoing savings projected at over $100 million annualized as we expand pilots.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Emily. Telehealth is transformative, now 28% of outpatient and 18% of total encounters, up significantly. It boosts access in rural areas, cuts LOS, and drives revenue through RPM for chronic care and Medicare Advantage. We expect 10-15% revenue uplift in 2025 from hybrid models, plus margin gains via productivity, as seen in our 22% tele-ICU coverage reducing locums.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Elena Vasquez:
Hi, Robert. Our $250 million Apex Digital Health Platform over 18 months integrates Epic with Nuance ambient AI, cutting documentation 30% and boosting productivity 15%. Partnerships like Google Cloud for predictive LOS, da Vinci for 10% surgical uplift, and Vizient GPO extend to tech synergies. These target $200 million cost savings and new streams from value-based telepsych/home health JVs.

Operator:
Thank you for the questions. This concludes the question-and-answer session.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
